A simple staircase diagram showing the progression from first use to addiction. Five steps rising from left to right: step 1 a young person being offered a substance by a friend ("Experimental use"), step 2 a party scene ("Occasional use"), step 3 a person alone using a substance ("Regular use"), step 4 the person taking a larger amount ("Tolerance: needs more"), step 5 the person looking distressed and shaking ("Dependence and addiction"). A small side panel shows a down arrow. Soft muted colours, no real drug brand names.

A four-panel classification chart of abused drugs. Panel 1 "Stimulants": simple icons of a coffee cup, a kolanut pod with nuts, a cigarette, a small white powder heap and clear crystal shards. Panel 2 "Depressants": a beer bottle and palm wine gourd, a tablet blister pack, a glue tube. Panel 3 "Narcotics (opioids)": a poppy flower with seed pod, a cough syrup bottle without brand, a tablet strip, a syringe. Panel 4 "Hallucinogens": a cannabis leaf and a mushroom. Each panel in a different soft colour. No brand names.

A circular "web of effects" diagram with a central figure of a young person surrounded by a drug symbol (an unbranded pill and bottle). Arrows lead outwards to eight round icons: a brain with a crack ("Mental illness"), lungs with dark patches ("Lung disease"), a heart with a jagged line ("Heart attack"), a liver ("Liver damage"), a syringe with a virus ("HIV and hepatitis"), a wrecked car ("Road accidents"), a broken house ("Family breakdown"), a school building with an exit arrow ("School dropout"), and a handcuff icon ("Crime"). Soft muted colours.
